$comment: Ranking weights, in one place. Section 46 asks for configurable weights and no hardcoding — every consumer reads a profile from here rather than carrying its own numbers, so a change to how ShopiQ ranks is a change to this file.

shopping.$comment: The requirement-driven search profile. These are the weights the recommendation engine has used since Phase 2 and they sum to 100, which several assertions depend on. Change them deliberately.

discovery.$comment: For 'show me some good laptops' — no stated budget, no stated use case. Section 52: with nothing specific to match, precision has nothing to work with, so quality and value carry more and diversity is widened.

accessory.$comment: For ranking things to go WITH something else. Relationship strength and fit dominate; the shopper's original budget is about the anchor, not the extras, so it barely applies.

$comment_signals: What each signal means, so a weight change is an informed one.

signals.budget: How comfortably the price sits inside a stated budget. Full marks anywhere under it; falls away above it rather than cutting off, so a near miss can still be shown and labelled.
signals.useCase: Overlap between what the shopper said they would do and what the product declares it suits.
signals.specification: How well real spec values meet stated constraints. Read from product_specs, never inferred.
signals.preference: Soft leanings — lighter, longer battery, better camera.
signals.rating: Customer rating, damped by review count so one five-star review does not outrank fifty four-star ones.
signals.value: Price against what comparable products in the same category cost. Rewards the honest deal, not the cheapest thing.
signals.relationship: Strength of the declared pairing: an explicit product relationship beats a category rule, which beats a bare category match.
signals.compatibility: Whether the attributes actually fit. A hard exclusion, not a weight, when a claim says not_compatible_with.
signals.priceProportion: Whether an accessory costs a sensible fraction of its anchor.
signals.availability: In stock, and how much. Out of stock is excluded before ranking rather than scored low.

$comment_guardrails: Section 45: no single signal may decide the outcome on its own.

guardrails.$comment_share: No signal may contribute more than 40% of the achievable total in a profile. Validated on load — a profile that breaks this is a configuration error, because a 60% budget weight makes 'cheapest' the answer to every question.
guardrails.$comment_filters: These remove candidates rather than lowering them. A product that cannot be bought, cannot fit, or was explicitly refused must not appear at position four.
